Replay

Inspecting and branching local history

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Ownership and limitsHello integrationEditing a preview

Debug_Scrubber is an opt-in timeline dock for an offline developer workflow. Pause, inspect a retained frame, and either resume the original future or start an alternate branch. The widget reads frame copies and returns commands; the application owns the clock, presentation and decision to replace its timeline.

Odin
// Init once at a stable address; destroy before its owner leaves the tree.
debuggd.debug_scrubber_init(&scrubber, owner)

// Before advancing the local timeline:
switch debuggd.debug_scrubber_frame(&scrubber, &timeline) {
case .Inspect: // Save prior pause state, pause the clock, discard device edges.
case .Resume: // Restore prior pause state, clear accumulated time/device edges.
case .Branch:
    frame, ok := debuggd.debug_scrubber_read(&scrubber, &timeline)
    if ok {
        // Explicit application operation: initialize from this complete frame
        // under a new epoch, reset presentation at this tick, then leave inspection.
    }
case .Invalidated: // The source epoch/head changed; release the inspection pause.
case .None:
}

// While active, paint this value instead of the live head. Do not play its old
// one-shot events or feed its poses back into simulation.
frame, inspecting := debuggd.debug_scrubber_read(&scrubber, &timeline)

debuggd.debug_scrubber_end(&scrubber)     // Explicit reset/branch completion.
debuggd.debug_scrubber_destroy(&scrubber) // Teardown, including signal callables.

F10 and the Pause/Resume button enter or leave inspection. Drag the slider or use its ordinary keyboard controls to select a frame. Branch is a separate button. Godot's pressed signal is latched, so a complete click between render frames still reaches the application. Repeated clicks on the same button before a pump coalesce. Keep the widget at a stable address until destroy disconnects callbacks.

The slider stores relative offsets within at most 4096 retained slots. It does not convert absolute u64 ticks to floating point. replay.history_window scans bounded record metadata and includes the initial/corrected checkpoint. This differs from an audit window, which requires known generating inputs and a preceding frame. Tick zero, wrapped retention, nonzero checkpoints and the u64 boundary are valid.

Ownership and limits#

The owner must exclusively pause its local timeline while inspecting. Epoch/head changes invalidate the selection; the widget does not detect arbitrary same-head, same-epoch replacement or concurrent mutation. Session, Room and P2P runners are not paused, corrected or migrated by these controls. No network or administrative authority is implied. Use the separate read-only diagnostic overlay on live peers.

Resume retains the original timeline and confirmation frontier. Branching is an explicit local operation from a complete frame, including entity generations, cooldowns and RNG. The application must start a new presentation epoch and seed its journal at the branch tick; old effects must not be delivered again. This does not undo already committed external effects. It is not network recovery or a save format. The optional field editor below edits a copied local preview; the recording exporter saves the original replayable suffix.

Hello integration#

Replay Hello enables the dock alongside debug_enabled / REPLAY_DEBUG=1. F8 controls the older audit panel; the history dock remains available when that panel is hidden. Ordinary launches allocate no debugging components.

The example preserves an existing pause on Resume, paints historical entity views, and clears transient flashes when leaving inspection. Branching calls its existing complete-frame reset under a fresh epoch. Gameplay input held during inspection stays suppressed until released, preventing a slider/key gesture from leaking into the resumed or branched simulation. Inspection creates no catch-up backlog.

Run nix develop --command bash tests/replay_scrubber/run.sh for the core-backed native scene workflow, existing Hello/Loot regressions, rendered capture and WASM check. The dedicated fixture preserves prepared inputs, binaries' hashes and driver revisions. Broader editor workflows remain roadmap work.

The recorded native/Chrome gate also covers real browser keyboard, slider and button input with zero buffer-target conflicts. Focused slider arrow keys intentionally change the selected tick; they are not gameplay movement while inspecting. Browser acceptance checks held fire, and native acceptance checks both held movement and fire. Hello's muzzle flash now uses an immutable mesh to avoid the Polygon2D redraw issue exposed by this gate.

Editing a preview#

Debug_Field_Editor(State) adds a schema-derived field menu, value input, Apply and Reset. Hello enables it with the history dock. Fields include array leaves, entity IDs, counters, timers, enum names and authority-only values; the application provides its state validator to reject broken relationships such as a pool count that disagrees with its live slots.

Odin
editor: debuggd.Debug_Field_Editor(game.World)
debuggd.debug_field_editor_init(&editor, owner, game.network_state_valid)

// Before handling the scrubber action, including Branch:
action := debuggd.debug_scrubber_frame(&scrubber, &timeline)
debuggd.debug_field_editor_frame(&editor, &scrubber, &timeline)
frame, inspecting := debuggd.debug_field_editor_read(&editor)
// Paint frame while inspecting. On Branch, accept this complete frame under a
// new epoch. On Resume/Invalidated, restore the previous pause and input guard.
// On explicit reset/branch completion:
debuggd.debug_field_editor_end(&editor)
// At teardown, before freeing its owner:
debuggd.debug_field_editor_destroy(&editor)

Apply validates a candidate, then replaces only the preview. The original frame, retained timeline, confirmation frontier and journal stay unchanged. Reset restores the selected original frame; selecting another tick or leaving inspection discards edits. Branch uses the edited state with the selected original tick. Hello seeds a new presentation epoch without playing old effects and preserves the prior pause. The dirty flag means an edit was accepted since selection/reset, including an accepted value equal to its original value.

Values accept exact booleans, decimal or 0x integers, enum names or declared numeric values, numeric bit masks, and finite floats. The input is limited to 128 characters. Overflow, malformed text, illegal flags, inactive union fields and model-invalid candidates are rejected without changing the preview. Union tags are inspectable but read-only: changing variants needs a complete valid value. Single-field validation cannot perform a coordinated multi-field transaction.

The menu shows at most the first 2048 schema leaves and explicitly reports truncation. Its search is supplied by Godot's ordinary dropdown. Large models can build their own searchable editor on schema.field_index, schema.scalar_text and schema.edit_scalar. These helpers do not alter schema fingerprints or wire formats. The widget requires a complete authority schema and retains two frame copies; Apply also allocates one canonical payload and a typed candidate. It is intended for paused authoring, not a simulation tick or a live network peer.
